records.name: Gunars
records.facts_used: Gunars: The documented Gunnar family continues Old Norse Gunnarr. Its elements are gunnr, war, and herr, army or warrior. They explain the old compound’s linguistic history rather than asserting that a modern bearer is warlike. The Latvian Language Agency gives the exact rendering Gunnar → Gunars, citing page 234 of a 2022 manual. This dated record illustrates transmission between languages; it is not a first birth registration or proof of one borrowing route in every family.

records.uncertainties: Exact IcelandicGunars2022 or NorwegianGunnars2003 agency row; do not transfer longāGunārs/Gunāra dictionary alternatives to these independently documented renderings.

records.name: Vladilens
records.facts_used: Vladilens: The name family was formed by contracting parts of Vladimir Ilyich Lenin’s name. It belongs to modern commemorative name formation rather than one ancient Slavic compound. That history makes no claim about every modern bearer’s political views. Siliņš’s dictionary dates the use of Vladilens: 1924. This records use of the particular name in Latvia. The entry cannot automatically be transferred to similar spellings or treated as the moment the entire name family originated.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Siliņš p332 exact own1924. Kraus2013PDF16printed8 documents related RussianVladilen/Vladilena/Vladlen/Vladlena; no universal personal naming motive inferred. Petrovsky1966 original PDF p. 80/printed p. 79 visually checked: Vladilena feminine of Vladilen, Vladlena feminine of Vladlen; both male contractions explicitly from VladimirIlyichLenin. Exact Latvian bridge remains the separate agency/catalogue evidence.

records.name: Zenonas
records.facts_used: Zenonas: The family’s Greek base is Zēnōn, connected with Zēnos, a form of the name Zeus. It refers to a Greek deity’s name rather than a separate full sentence. The ancient root does not itself determine a modern bearer’s religion or character. The 1964 calendar reprinted in Salys’s 1983 volume gives Zenonas (Zenas) on 5 April. This is a concrete printed example of the form’s use. Its position in the historical calendar need not match every modern calendar and is not the name’s invention date.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: OriginalPDF305printed290Aprilheading and exactZenonasApril5. Historical date differs from suppliedDec8; no overwrite.

records.name: Külli
records.facts_used: Külli: The name belongs to the Külli/Külliki and Finnish Kyllikki group, associated with abundance and sufficiency words: Estonian küll and Finnish kyllä and kyllin. Sources describe both the local word connection and Finnish-form influence; one identical borrowing route need not be assumed for every family. The first page of Leole’s December 2005 issue uses the exact spelling Külli. The local name column shows that this form was discussed in Estonian print. This dated evidence is neither a first birth record nor the year the name was invented.
